thread:
ana: Quick follow-up on the on-prem upgrade RFC — ran into a race in staging where two operators tried to activate overlapping bundles during a canary. Did we lock the orchestrator delegation semantics down?

kevin: Saw that. My read: we left the operator lease model intentionally loose (short leases + heartbeat) but didn't define migration of responsibility during canary rollouts.

sam: Right — current flow is: controller A gets lease, pulls bundle, starts activation. Controller B can also get lease if A misses heartbeats. But during canary we had A still active while B started a partial activation. End result: two half-applied states.

michael: Options I sketched: 1) Strong single-master lease (longer TTL, explicit handoff API) 2) Coordinated staged activation protocol (leader proposes window, followers ack) 3) Activation idempotency+dry-run validation so dual activations are safe. Tradeoffs: 1 is simpler but brittle under operator flakiness; 2 is more complex but explicit; 3 is safest but requires more tooling and longer preflight.

lisa: For air-gapped installs we can't rely on fast RPCs between controllers (network might be flaky). Leaning away from heavy coordination (#2) unless we make it purely local to the cluster operator and fall back.

kevin: Agreed. Proposal: combine (1) + lightweight (3). Single active lease per cluster for activation windows, TTL ~5m, but every activation must include a signed dry-run manifest and a checksum validation step that can be applied safely multiple times. If a second controller tries to activate concurrently, it will detect checksum mismatch and either adopt or abort.

ana-ops-bot: deploy: canary rollout started for cluster-42 (bundle v1.3.7) — observing activation latency.

ana-ops-bot: alert: cluster-42 reported partial-activation on node-3 (operator A) — rollback triggered.

sam: I drafted a small manifest extension for the dry-run token and activation id. Example:```yaml
activation:
  id: "2026-03-01T15:12:03Z-ndx-42"
  dry_run_checksum: "sha256:3a7f..."
  operator_lease: 
    holder: "operator-a"
    lease_until: "2026-03-01T15:17:03Z"
  phase: "dry-run"
```This lets the second operator see a pending activation id and checksum and avoid starting a divergent apply.

michael: Nice. A couple of edge cases: what if operator A is hung but still reporting heartbeats? We need a forced takeover path. Suggest: takeover requires a signed takeover token from the control plane (for hosted) or an operator-local consensus: if heartbeat stale beyond a configurable extended TTL (e.g., 2x), controller B can create a takeover intent with its own signed activation.id and increment a takeover counter in the manifest. The apply logic enforces monotonic takeover counters.

lisa: For private/offline, control plane signed tokens are not available. We can instead rely on cluster-local monotonic sequence stored in the operator's raft/leader-store (or simple file-backed monotonic counter) — must be durable across restarts.

kevin: Implementation notes: - Keep the operator_lease short to allow recovery from lost nodes. - Persist activation.id + checksum atomically before any partial filesystem/activation step. - Provide an operator GET /activation/status endpoint that returns current activation.id, phase, checksum, and takeover_counter. - Add a strict apply preflight: if incoming activation.id != persisted id and takeover_counter <= persisted, abort and report.
